answer:
Use `FunctionAgent`, the prebuilt agent in LlamaIndex. The docs say that "To create an agent in LlamaIndex, it takes only a few lines of code:" [llama_index/docs/src/content/docs/framework/module_guides/deploying/agents/index.md]. Its example imports it with `from llama_index.core.agent.workflow import FunctionAgent` [llama_index/docs/src/content/docs/framework/module_guides/deploying/agents/index.md]. You pass your tools and an LLM to it, along with a system prompt. The example uses `tools=[multiply],` and `llm=OpenAI(model="gpt-4o-mini")` [llama_index/docs/src/content/docs/framework/module_guides/deploying/agents/index.md].

Tools are ordinary Python functions with a docstring that describes what they do. The example defines `multiply(a: float, b: float) -> float` with the docstring "Useful for multiplying two numbers." [llama_index/docs/src/content/docs/framework/module_guides/deploying/agents/index.md]. The tool name and description matter because the LLM relies on them to choose a tool and write its arguments [llama_index/docs/src/content/docs/framework/module_guides/deploying/agents/tools.md].

For more custom control, the docs point to Workflows: "LlamaIndex Workflows allow you to build very custom, agentic workflows through a core event-driven orchestration foundation." [llama_index/docs/src/content/docs/framework/use_cases/agents.md]

The excerpts don't show how to run the agent (the exact call for executing a query), so I don't know those details from this context. Check the full agent guide for that.
